title: Bylaw Provision on Class Combinations — One Holding per Class and a Change of Member Segment, Member Equities & Patronage
content:
All of a member's amounts in one Member Equities & Patronage class are pooled in a single holding, so a second holding of a class the member already holds in subscribed, active or retirement requested status is never opened; new amounts are booked to the existing holding.

## 1. One holding per class

1.1 A second holding of a class the member already holds in subscribed, active or retirement requested status is never opened.

1.2 The test is made on the association's own record of the member's holdings — the member, the class and the holding's status — before a subscription is opened, and it binds the member and the class of the subscription being opened. New amounts in that class (a purchase, retained patronage, a reinvested dividend) are booked to the holding that already exists.

## 2. Borrower equity classes exclude one another

2.1 The three borrower equity classes exclude one another: a member holds only the one matching the member's primary segment under the segments to which each class is issued — the Class C Participation Certificate for a rural homeowner, the Class A Nonvoting Common Stock for an agribusiness member, the Class B Voting Stock for a farm operator.

2.2 When the member's segment changes (a rural homeowner who starts farming in their own right, for example), the old class is retired at par and the same amount is purchased in the new class on the same day, the retirement being recorded with the reason redemption and the payment method deducted from proceeds, so the borrower stock requirement stays met without any cash changing hands.

## 3. Classes held alongside borrower equity

Allocated surplus and preferred stock may be held alongside any borrower equity class.

## Desk notes (hypothetical cases)

- A member with an active Qualified Allocated Surplus holding receives a new patronage allocation: the retained amount is booked to the existing Qualified Allocated Surplus holding; no second holding is opened.
- A rural homeowner holding a Class C Participation Certificate of USD 600.00 starts farming in their own right. On one day the certificate is retired at par for USD 600.00 with the reason redemption and payment method deducted from proceeds, and USD 600.00 of Class B Voting Stock is purchased. The member pays nothing and receives nothing.
